h1:
Khao Yai Pomelo & Khom Lychee
Brackish-Orchard Fruit of Mae Klong
intro: Samut Songkhram is a tiny province with rich soil because it sits at the mouth of the Mae Klong River. The water in the orchards is brackish, rising and falling with the tide and carrying mineral sediment into the groves every single day. The two fruits this province is proudest of are Khao Yai pomelo and Khom lychee — both hold GI status, and you can buy them straight from the source orchards if you time your visit right.

blocks.html: Samut Songkhram's provincial motto includes the line 'town of razor clams, finest lychee' — a clear sign that fruit here is genuinely renowned, not just a souvenir afterthought. What makes it special is that the orchards around Amphawa and Mae Klong sit in brackish-water territory, where the tides push minerals — calcium, phosphorus, iron — into the groves daily. The resulting fruit carries a taste and aroma that's hard to replicate anywhere else. So we want to walk you through what to eat, what to buy, and when to drop by the orchards to get the best of it.

blocks.text: Why Mae Klong fruit tastes different

blocks.html: The key is the word 'brackish.' The orchards in Amphawa and Mae Klong sit near the river mouth, so the water in the irrigation channels is fresh water mixed with a little salt, rising and falling with the tide twice a day. The mineral-rich estuary silt keeps the trees healthy and gives the fruit a deep, distinctive flavor. This is exactly why Mae Klong's Khao Yai pomelo and Khom lychee earned GI registration (Geographical Indication) — meaning the genuine article can only come from this area.

items: Tidal brackish water — carries mineral sediment into the orchards every day, keeping trees healthy and the fruit deeply flavored
GI-certified — both Khao Yai pomelo and Khom lychee are registered, so the real thing comes only from Samut Songkhram
Still handmade — many are old family orchards, some trees decades old, all hand-picked and hand-sorted

blocks.text: Khao Yai pomelo — thin skin, big segments, year-round

blocks.html: Khao Yai pomelo is available almost all year, but the sweetest, most abundant stretch is roughly October to December. The standout traits: a fairly thin, easy-to-peel skin, large segments in a whitish-yellow, few seeds, and a sweet-tart balance that's spot on without any lingering bitterness. Walk through Amphawa Floating Market or Mae Klong Market and you'll see it sold whole as well as peeled and bagged ready to eat.

items: Peak season — October to December: sweetest and most plentiful (it's sold at other times too, just in smaller quantities)
What a good one looks like — thin skin, smooth surface, heavy for its size, firm whitish-yellow segments, few seeds
Farm price — Grade A runs about ฿50–65 per kilo, or buy a set of 2–3 fruits with delivery

blocks.title: How to pick a good pomelo
blocks.html: Lift a few and compare by size — the one that's heavier for its size usually holds more juice. The skin should be smooth and taut, not wrinkled. Press gently on the base; if it's firm and not soft or spongy, it's still fresh. If the orchard offers a taste before you buy, taste first and then decide, because sweetness varies by tree and by harvest window.

blocks.text: Khom lychee — the heaven-sent fruit, once a year

blocks.html: Khom lychee is a rarity that Mae Klong locals are deeply proud of. It's nicknamed the 'heaven-sent fruit' because how much it yields depends on the weather each year — some years the trees are loaded, some years there's almost nothing. The original cultivar was brought to Amphawa back in the reign of King Rama IV; it was first called 'i-khom' because the trees were short, then politely shortened to 'khom.' The marks of the real thing: standing spines, taut skin, plump flesh, a deep-red to dark-crimson shell, whitish-pink flesh that's dry rather than wet, sweet and fragrant with a faint astringency at the tip of the tongue. It measures around 19–20 Brix, which counts as very sweet.

items: Very short season — around mid-April to May (the first batch usually lands around Songkran); miss it this year and you wait until next
How to spot the real thing — standing spines, taut skin, plump flesh, dark-crimson shell, whitish-pink flesh, dry not wet
Limited supply — some years the whole province yields only a few tons, so it costs more than ordinary lychee; pre-ordering is the surer bet

blocks.title: To catch Khom lychee in season
blocks.html: In April the province usually holds a Khom Lychee and Mae Klong Produce festival, where many orchards sell side by side — the easiest time all year to buy. If you can't make the festival, call the orchard first to ask whether the fruit is ripe, because it sells out extremely fast.

blocks.text: Roadside orchards you can stop at

blocks.html: The densest cluster of fruit orchards is around Khwae Om subdistrict in Amphawa, along a road locals call 'Fruit Orchard Road,' where old groves line up one after another. Many open for farm-gate sales, and some let you walk through or pick your own. Before you go, call ahead to check whether the fruit is ripe and which days the orchard is open, since the harvest follows the season and some days they're closed.

items.name: Yutthasuwan Orchard (Amphawa)
items.blurb: A Khao Yai pomelo orchard selling straight from the grove, around ฿65 per kilo, with delivery available — good for buying a gift box.

items.name: Thanomjit Orchard (Amphawa)
items.blurb: A pomelo orchard run on GAP standards with a focus on fruit quality; a favorite stop for handpicking good-looking pomelos.

items.name: Lung Wichian Orchard (Amphawa)
items.blurb: A Khom lychee orchard around Amphawa, fruiting in the April–May season; sells at the gate when it's in, so call to check before you go.

items.name: Pa Lek Orchard / Khwae Om Fruit Orchard Road
items.blurb: An old orchard district where some lychee trees are decades old; you can browse several groves along one road, best visited in lychee season.

blocks.title: Straight talk before you drive out to the orchards
blocks.html: Orchard fruit really does follow the season — come outside lychee season and there will be none to buy, guaranteed. Pomelo is around almost all year, but the late-year peak is when it's sweetest and cheapest. Many orchards are family-run and not open as a shop every day, so call ahead to avoid a wasted trip.

blocks.text: Buying at the market vs. at the orchard

items: Amphawa Floating Market / Mae Klong Market — convenient and easy, sold peeled and bagged ready to eat; good if you just want a taste while you're out exploring
Roadside orchard gate — fresh fruit you pick yourself, usually a better price, plus you can chat with the owner about the harvest window
Annual fruit festival — many orchards in one place, ideal in April when Khom lychee is in season and easiest to find
Order by post — many orchards pack boxes and ship nationwide, good if you live far away or want to send a gift

faq.q: When is Samut Songkhram's Khao Yai pomelo on sale?
faq.a: Khao Yai pomelo is on sale almost all year, but the sweetest and most abundant stretch is roughly October to December. Prices are good then and you can pick the best fruit. Grade A from the orchard runs about 50–65 THB per kilo.

faq.q: Which month does Khom lychee come out, and why is it called the heaven-sent fruit?
faq.a: Khom lychee comes out around mid-April to May, with the first batch usually arriving around Songkran — a very short season. It's called the heaven-sent fruit because how much it yields depends on the weather each year: some years it's loaded, some years there's almost nothing. It's hard to control, so you're at the mercy of the rains and the skies.

faq.q: Why does Samut Songkhram fruit taste better than elsewhere?
faq.a: Because the orchards around Amphawa and Mae Klong sit in brackish-water territory, where the tides push mineral sediment into the groves every day. The soil is rich, so the fruit develops a flavor and aroma all its own — enough to earn GI registration.

faq.q: Do I need to call ahead to buy from an orchard?
faq.a: You should always call to check first, especially in lychee season, because the fruit follows the season and sells out fast. Many orchards are family-run and not open every day, so calling ahead saves you a wasted trip and gets you fresh fruit straight off the tree.

faq.q: When should I go if I want Khom lychee that's easy to find?
faq.a: In April the province usually holds a Khom Lychee and Mae Klong Produce festival, with many orchards selling side by side — the easiest time all year to buy. It's ideal if you'd rather not drive from orchard to orchard.
